institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. "Adventure": I found Paris to be a very exciting city to live in, where I could practice my french and get to live in an iconic capital with many cultural offers like museums, restaurants, music etc.
1. "Academic opportunity": SciencesPo Paris is a great university for political science, so that also played a very important role for me when i choose my study destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I think the university send out a lot of e-mails in advance and their student website was okay easy to navigate

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had arranged a welcome week program, which was great both as a pratical introduction (where is the campus, how does the printer work etc.), as an academic introduction (how to write assignments at SciencesPo) and as a social introduction (meet french students and exchange students)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me. I had known quite a few studens who went on exchange to Paris before me, and they all recommended me to apply to the Danish House in the Cité Universitaire, so I did that and got accepted. Hereafter I got moved to the Mexican house in the Cité, as a part of an exchange program in the Cité Universitaire, but that was also just fine

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Great idea to apply to a house in the Cité Universitaire. It is close to the city, has affordable housing and provides great social activities. If students chooses to find an apartment in the city they should be aware of scams etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A few weeks in advance we were given information on how to register. However, as an exchange student our registration opened later than registration for "normal" students, which meant we could only choose between "left over" courses/there were very few spots available, which I think was a shame. Further, it was very stressful because the registration was based on a "first come - first served" base. Personally, I think making a priority list of courses works better.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a zoom presentation one could join + information on e-mail, which got send out in advance of the registration

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any of the classes I wanted. Each time I clicked on a class to register I realized it was full, and in the mean time the other classes I wanted also got filled up.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be very fast with registration and have a plan a-z, because you can't at all count on getting the classes you want

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was very fitting

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was in general very similar to the style of teaching at UCPH. The classes consisted of app. 20-30 students and had an open environment for debate, while the lectures of app. 200-300 students were very similar to those of UCPH, where the communication is more top-down with the prof lecturing and less interaction. However, a difference I noticed was that the students seemed to get a bigger say in the smaller classes than they do a UCPH - e.g., in two of my classes the students had a say in the exam format, when deadlines were set etc., which I think is more set from the beginning at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. GENDER, SOCIETIES AND ECONOMICS
2. CHINESE POLITICAL CULTURE THROUGH HISTORY: AN ECOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVE
3. GENDER AND REVOLUTIONARY SITUATIONS IN THE MIDDLE EAST
4. DISCRIMINATION AND INEQUALITY IN COMPARATIVE PERSPECTIVES: THEORIES, EVIDENCE AND POLICIES
5. THE SYRIAN CRISIS AND ITS CONSEQUENCES FOR EUROPE AND THE MIDDLE EAST (2011-2023)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the course on the Syrian Crisis and its consequences. I liked it for three main reasons: 1) It was super well structured starting from the Ottoman Empire up untill today, 2) It dealt with several aspects of the crisis - e.g., the international aspect, the refugee aspect and the domestic aspect and 3) The teacher had a great deal of knowledge on the topic and was very engaged in the course.

questions.answer: I didn't really experience any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I found the supermarkets to more expensive than I had expected + going out (e.g., buying beer, wine, entrance to nightclubs etc)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot! There was so many associations that I can't even list them all, but the activities ranged from parties, wine tastings and interesting talks to going to sports like dance, tennis, soccer etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed going to interesting talks with prominent politicians, academics or people working in the field (e.g., NGOs, UN institutions etc). I thought is was a super nice way to arrange an interesting night. Often I combined it with going out to dinner with friends, so it was a nice way to gather around a common interlecual  interest

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of fun stuff to do in Paris during weekends and holidays. 
During weekends I loved visiting museums (both the popular ones like Louvre, d'Orsay etc, but also less famous ones like l'Orangerie, Petit Palais and Rodin). Further, there is a lot of nice restaurants, open air markets etc, which is also nice to do in a weekend, and finally its wonderfull just to take a stroll in the many amazing Paris districts - my favorite is probably the 10th arrondissement! 
On holidays I will recommend maybe going out of the city - the TGV trains are super fast and well connected to nice cities in France. I did a hike in the Normandy from the city of Fécamp til Ètretat that I can really recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, but I think that France and Denmark is also very much a like, so that wasn't a big problem.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: "Unfortunately" I mainly socialized with other exchange students living in the Cité Universitaire like me. Hence I don't have any great tips on making local friends, but it was still an amazing experience getting to know other exchange students from a wide range of countries.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't really find any cultural differences challenging, but of course language was sometimes a barrier, even though I found that Parisians spoke better english than what people normally say

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I just love the french food- and going out culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare for a big workload. You often hear that exchange is "easy" in terms of workload, but that is not at all my experience. I found the academic level very high, and had a lot of assignments during the semester, but on the postive side, I had a shorter exam period in the end, because I had handed in a lot of papers during the semester. 
2. Be fast with course registration! The courses fill up quickly
3. Don't be afraid to engage in the courses. The courses a very much based on student participation, so it is very rewarding to participate actively in the classes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I you want to apply for french language courses at the university be aware that the level (in my opinion) is very high. I took one class in french level B1, and found that that level was higher than what I had expected

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a lot of amazing fellow exchange students and trying to live in such a wonderful city as Paris

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing workload+wanting to do good in school, while at the same time allowing yourself to also spend time on seeing Paris and take the time off to do that

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
